name: Drooling Face
baseMeaning: A face with drool coming from its mouth, signaling hunger or desire.
tldr: 🤤 means hunger or desire, but in playful chats it often means being completely exhausted or overwhelmed.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🤤 directly shows that someone is hungry, tempted by food, or salivating over something they want.
In close friend groups, 🤤 is a cartoon way to say you are so tired that you have completely checked out.
contextMeanings.example: after that meeting i am completely 🤤

contextMeanings.meaning: 🤤 can jokingly mean that something is so good you cannot properly react to it.
A work-thread 🤤 can suggest exhaustion, but its cartoonish drool may also make the sender look as if they have lost their composure.
contextMeanings.example: that call wrecked me, i am still 🤤

platformNotes.note: 🤤 fits comfortably in iMessage conversations with friends, family, or a partner because those threads often use playful cartoon reactions. It works best when everyone already knows the message is about being exhausted or completely enchanted.

In Instagram direct messages, 🤤 can come across as performative rather than naturally funny, especially in a close thread where exaggerated reactions are common. A quieter tired emoji may suit the exchange better.
Slack gives 🤤 a strong work setting, where the drool can make a coworker look as if they have abandoned professionalism. It is safer among familiar teammates than in a customer-facing channel.

WhatsApp threads with family and international friends can accommodate the playful meaning when the relationship supports it. In more formal family conversations, the literal drooling image may be clearer than the tired joke.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z commonly uses 🤤 as the cartoon choice for being knocked out, often with the same dramatic exhaustion behind 😩 or 😫.
Millennials are more likely to choose 😪 or 😴 for ordinary tiredness, while 🤤 can still land as a playful, deliberately excessive reaction.
A Boomer may take 🤤 more literally and hear hunger, thirst, or someone who is unwell. Its intended tired joke may not land without context.

warnings.title: Too cartoonish for formal work
warnings.description: In a work thread or customer-facing reply, 🤤 can make the sender look as if they have stopped pretending to be professional. Use 😪, 😴, or plain words when composure matters.

warnings.title: The joke may be too much for the relationship
warnings.description: With a mid-tier friend, the exaggerated drool can feel childish rather than affectionate. A simple “I’m exhausted” is less likely to misfire.

seoDescription: What does 🤤 mean? It can signal hunger or desire, but in playful chats it often means being completely exhausted or overwhelmed by something good.

longForm.overview:
🤤 arrived on the keyboard in Unicode 9.0 in 2016. Its original image is deliberately crude: half-closed eyes and a little drool running from the mouth. That picture began with the most direct meaning—someone is hungry,欲望 has taken over, or food looks impossibly good—but the drool was also perfect for the cartoon image of a person who has been knocked out cold. Before long, chat threads were using 🤤 for that exhausted state as well.

Today, the tired meaning often hides the literal one. “goodnight 🤤” says “I am so tired I am practically unconscious,” while “this show has me 🤤” says “this is so good I cannot even respond normally.” That is what separates 🤤 from 😴, which plainly means sleep, 🥱, which suggests boredom or fighting sleep, and 😩, which expresses dramatic exhaustion. 🤤 goes further: it turns being finished into a drooling cartoon image. The joke works best when the relationship and tone already allow exaggerated playfulness.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🤤 often appears after a draining meeting, a long day, or a late night with a partner. In a coworker’s Slack thread, “after that meeting I am 🤤” says the meeting left the sender unable to think. Among close friends, the same emoji can describe being overwhelmed by a show: “this show has me 🤤” means the recommendation is so good that words have become useless.

Its original appetite meaning is still alive. People use 🤤 beside pictures of food, restaurant menus, or an especially desirable person. In those messages, no explanation is needed because the drool does the work. The shift from “I want that” to “I am completely done” depends on the sentence around it.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Avoid 🤤 in customer support, formal workplace messages, or any conversation where professionalism matters. The cartoon drool can make a work thread look unserious and a brand-facing reply look as if it has lost control of its voice. It can also age the sender in a mid-tier friendship, where 😩 may already feel excessive.

Do not send it when discussing illness, exhaustion, or something genuinely distressing unless that is the shared joke. People may read the drool literally or take it as a sign that you are not taking the problem seriously. In serious situations, use words, 😪, or 😴 instead. Even with an older relative, expect that 🤤 may be understood as literal hunger rather than a clever tired reaction.
longForm.howToReply:
Match the intended joke first. If someone says they are 🤤 after a difficult day, reply with “go sleep” or another tired emoji. If they send 🤤 about a show or meal, respond to the thing they are excited about rather than treating it as a request for help. Mirroring 🤤 can work when the relationship is close and the exchange is already playful.

If the drool lands badly, a brief “Too much?” often clears it up better than a long explanation. If you used 🤤 and someone calls it childish or unprofessional, switch to plain language: “That meeting knocked me out” or “I’m completely exhausted.” That keeps the meaning while removing the cartoonish part that caused the problem.

faqs.question: What does 🤤 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: It can mean he is knocked out from exhaustion, salivating over food, or very attracted to you. The surrounding message usually makes the intended meaning clear.

faqs.question: Is 🤤 flirty?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. “You look 🤤” can express intense attraction, but 🤤 also appears as a tired joke or a reaction to food, so it is not flirty by itself.

faqs.question: What does 🤤 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: In playful TikTok comments, it often means being completely overwhelmed by something good, or being so exhausted that you have checked out. Literal hunger remains possible too.

faqs.question: What does 🤤 mean in a work chat?
faqs.answer: It likely means the sender is exhausted, though the cartoonish drool can make them seem less professional. A plain sentence is safer in formal channels.

conversationExamples.message: that three hour meeting actually ended me, i am still 🤤
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender means the meeting left them mentally finished. In a casual coworker thread, reply with sympathy; in a formal channel, plain words about fatigue will work better.

conversationExamples.message: you looked so good last night, i was basically 🤤
conversationExamples.interpretation: Here the drool expresses attraction and being overwhelmed by the other person’s appearance. A warm reply can keep the flirtation going without escalating the sexual tone.

conversationExamples.message: bro this new show has me 🤤 every episode
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is saying the show is so good that they can barely react to it. Ask which episode they are on or tease them about being completely absorbed.

conversationExamples.message: goodnight 🤤 i barely made it to bed
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a playful way to say the day left them so tired that they are practically unconscious. Reply with a simple goodnight rather than treating the drool as a medical concern.

conversationExamples.message: look at this dumpling place, i am fully 🤤
conversationExamples.interpretation: The original appetite meaning is doing the work: the sender wants the food badly. Reacting to the food or sending your own hungry emoji keeps the exchange obvious.
